scenes.setting: Evernight Demonic Wolf and the Goddess connect in Klein's mind; The World's follow-up buys the body-spirit-switching puzzle: not Phoenix (Death) pathway — likely a Mutant, Sequence 9 'Prisoner' of the Rose School of Thought; the gathering closes
scenes.text_anchor: “In the City of Silver, the corresponding Sequence 9 is called Prisoner.

scenes.setting: Above the fog (visions only: an Abraham-family youth losing control into crawling flesh, congealing into the Master Key beside a diamond-set pocket watch): the key's origin divined; Fors's 430-pound sacrifice arrives, Justice's diary offer is declined, and The Sun's memories are 'awakened'
scenes.text_anchor: “Ancestors, I am about to embark on the path of extraordinariness.

scenes.setting: City of Silver: Derrick maps the Seven Gods to the ancient gods, heads for the twin-tower library — and Elder Lovia lifts the creation-myth book from his hands, acting perfectly, terrifyingly normal
scenes.text_anchor: “Greetings, Elder Lovia.”

scenes.setting: The dossier holds no animal records: Klein plants the idea by letter to Isengard ('did he practice on animals?'), and mailbox loitering earns him a straight-faced dinner invitation from Jurgen — grandmother's cooking and cat included
scenes.text_anchor: “Why don't you come to my house as a guest?

scenes.setting: Night at the Harvest Church: behind a sealed stone door rants the Master Key's previous owner — a Sanguine who got lost into the cathedral mid-bloodthirst and now endures scripture; he'll reveal the key's origin 'if you rescue me first'
scenes.text_anchor: “He is the original owner of the Master Key.

scenes.setting: The Mental Terror Candle threat loosens the vampire's tongue: the Master Key came from a thief's haul at a south-bridge house; a coin catches his lying address, the real one is 32 Verdi Street — 'Remember, my name is Emlyn White!'
scenes.text_anchor: “Remember that my name is Emlyn White.

scenes.setting: A secluded corner: the pendulum rates Verdi Street 'somewhat dangerous' — postponed until purifying bullets are in hand, minting the Magician's first rule: never perform unprepared
scenes.text_anchor: “Never perform unprepared!”

scenes.setting: Tuesday breakfast with Stuart's report: both watched suspects are placidly ordinary; Klein thanks him off the case and sets out for the Roselle Memorial Exhibition
scenes.text_anchor: It's from Stuart…

scenes.setting: Dressed in lace and snow-white fur for the exhibition, Audrey is upgraded by her father to a private after-hours viewing — perfect for studying Roselle's diaries up close
scenes.text_anchor: “Father, I plan to attend the Roselle Memorial Exhibition.”

scenes.setting: The Roselle Memorial Exhibition: gold toilets, plagiarized Yeats, Chinese-chess 'inventions' — a tall veiled lady lingers over the children's exhibits — and in the restored study, bookmarks everywhere: one manuscript pile bears a bookmark painted with Roselle in emperor's clothes
scenes.text_anchor: Roselle had once disguised a Card of Blasphemy as a bookmark and placed it inside a certain book!

scenes.setting: Casing the study exhibit: elimination logic says only the 'manuscript of creativity' is valuable enough for Roselle's joke — its emperor-portrait bookmark may be the second Card of Blasphemy; security is light with the Devil hunt on, and the washroom recon completes the floor plan
scenes.text_anchor: There's only one bookmark in the entire exhibition hall that requires verification.

scenes.setting: Home scheming with image intact: Klein prays to himself as 'the adorer' — touch the bookmark, nick it, whisper 'Pirate King' in Hermes, 500 pounds — then above the fog forwards the mosaicked plea to Miss Justice without Mr. Fool saying a word
scenes.text_anchor: He decided to pass on the image and voice of his “adorer's” plea directly to Miss Justice.

scenes.setting: At her dressing table Audrey receives the fog-borne plea and Mr. Fool's five words — 'You can choose to accept this request or not' — and plots her museum performance around a needle-tipped gemstone earring and Susie
scenes.text_anchor: “You can choose to accept this request or not.”

scenes.setting: Audrey's private evening tour: curiosity spread evenly from the golden toilet to the diary, Machinery Hivemind captain Max Livermore approving each touch — then Susie's bark, an earring-needle prick, 'Pirate King' in two tongues, and an unmistakable resistance. Report to The Fool: 'It had an abnormal reaction.'
scenes.text_anchor: When the sharp, needle-like accessory touched the surface of the bookmark

scenes.setting: Above the fog: Justice's astonishing same-day confirmation seals it — a Card of Blasphemy; Klein plans a tonight-heist that steals broadly (bookmark AND books) so suspicion can never land on her
scenes.text_anchor: It would be best if I take action tonight!

scenes.setting: Museum defenses: rooftop watchers, patrol rotations, a building-block Sealed Artifact that traps intruders inside — and Roselle's diary left as deliberate bait for 'free meritorious deeds'
scenes.text_anchor: “Who wouldn't want free meritorious deeds?”

scenes.setting: 18 King's Avenue storage room: body parked behind Holy Night Powder seals, Klein ghosts out as a whistle-hardened spirit, paint-faced, drifting through walls to the museum — a matchbox through the washroom vent, then up to the second floor
scenes.text_anchor: “Action time!”

scenes.setting: The matchbox blaze in the washroom springs the defenders: guards rush the fire, the two watchers hold the diary hall per orders, and Max sprints back confident the block-model artifact will cage any intruder
scenes.text_anchor: “Once you enter, you will be like prey that has fallen into a trap!”

scenes.setting: The spirit-ghost descends into the study and palms both bookmarks — then baby wails, frozen air, eyeballs of squirming worms, and a soft voice from atop the bookshelves: 'Why did you only take the bookmarks?' Klein smiles wide — and vanishes
scenes.text_anchor: “Why did you only take the bookmarks? Where did you learn to only take the bookmarks?”

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog, the escape hatch that needs no escape: ending the self-summoning yanked spirit, whistle and bookmarks clean out of the world — while Max stares at a model that never gained a red dot
scenes.text_anchor: “Fortunately, I was prepared.”

scenes.setting: Back in his body and Master-Keying homeward through the terraces — until a wall opens onto a blood stench: a woman gutted on the living-room floor, organs gone, and grunting close by
scenes.text_anchor: The strong smell of blood! Klein frowned.

scenes.setting: The twelfth crime scene, mid-feast: a black dog balloons into a winged, horned Devil — its 'Die!' burns a paper substitute rusty, its delayed fireball shatters the street, and Klein escapes through an illusion, a fireplace Flaming Jump, and good old screams of 'Murder!'
scenes.text_anchor: It really is an animal! It's a Sequence 6 Devil

scenes.setting: The getaway carriage climbs a road of pea vines into the sky: the museum woman, black boots dangling from a vine hammock, interrogates him — truthful answers pass her invisible search, and she leaves a warning: the Master Key carries a curse
scenes.text_anchor: “That key has a certain curse. It must not be used unless absolutely necessary.”

scenes.setting: Morning headlines scream 'The twelfth case!' while the museum theft gets a blurb; behind bathroom steam Klein ascends and finally holds the emperor-figured bookmark: 'It really wasn't easy getting you!'
scenes.text_anchor: Klein sat down and picked up the bookmark that depicted the figure of Emperor Roselle.

scenes.setting: Cracking the card above the fog: not 'Pirate King', not 'One Piece' — 'Bernadette' in ancient Feysac wakes it, unveiling Sequence 0 DARK EMPEROR and the full Lawyer-to-god pathway with formulas and the nine-mausoleum apotheosis ritual; then a calm reply to Justice: 'That was a Card of Blasphemy made by Roselle.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Sequence 0: Dark Emperor!”

scenes.setting: Grace at the Hall table interrupted twice by the fog: 'Card of Blasphemy' and a 3000-pound thank-you from the 'adorer'; over breakfast Count Hall relays the twelfth murder and the comic eyewitness who fled screaming — Audrey wishes that poor man sweet dreams
scenes.text_anchor: “That was a Card of Blasphemy made by Roselle.”

scenes.setting: The looted study: Archbishop Horamick Haydn clears the aristocratic visitors, reads two opposed intruders in the residue — one perhaps above his own Sequence — and grasps the truth: 'We've been tricked by Roselle for more than 150 years…'
scenes.text_anchor: “We've been tricked by Roselle for more than 150 years…”

scenes.setting: Aftermath housekeeping: the Dark Emperor card and Master Key stored above the fog, the escape reviewed clue by clue — and a fresh letter from Isengard Stanton waits in the mailbox
scenes.text_anchor: The letter was from Isengard Stanton.

scenes.setting: Isengard's letter confirms the sweep worked: the missing strays, and the suspect boy from four years ago who kept a large black dog no one saw again after his 'death'; Klein replies humbly and hands the hunt to the officials
scenes.text_anchor: he was quite fond of animals, especially a large black dog.

scenes.setting: A quiet Wednesday at the Quelaag Club: Talim's guarded 'I have a friend in love with someone he shouldn't be' consultation ends in confidentiality — with both agreeing best-seller romances read nothing like real people
scenes.text_anchor: “I have a friend who has fallen in love with someone he shouldn't have.

scenes.setting: Lunch with a crutch-bound Aaron Ceres: botched operations, a train accident, burglary, broken leg — the surgeon begs for a 'capable fortune-teller', and Klein hears echoes of the Misfortune Cloth Puppet
scenes.text_anchor: “Do you think someone has cursed me?”

scenes.setting: The curse consult: no lost blood, no unlucky family — only a hospitalized boy, Will Auceptin, who drew the reversed Wheel of Fortune and smiled 'Doctor, your luck will get worse'; Klein steers Aaron toward his church so the Nighthawks will notice
scenes.text_anchor: “His name is Will Auceptin.

scenes.setting: The Rice Circus small theater: a heckler announces what the black bear, tiger and baboon are really thinking — the trainer stiffens, and Klein finds the chubby-faced voice oddly familiar
scenes.text_anchor: “I say, this guy wanted to give you a slap just a moment ago!”

scenes.setting: Dream-recall places the heckler: the Apothecary from Eye of Wisdom's gatherings; the stage magician's misdirection fools even a Seer's eyes, seeding the Magician's second and third rules — command attention, earn the applause
scenes.text_anchor: The Magician's second rule is fully divert a target's attention

scenes.setting: Yanked into a Beyonders-only battle layer mid-carriage-ride: soulless illusion-passengers all around as the Churches execute the Devil dog under a devouring moon-light — Klein hides behind a paper double, hears one furious snort from an unseen watcher, and the shattered void returns him to reality
scenes.text_anchor: the gigantic Devil dog would be discovered, executed, and cleansed!

chapters_detail.title: He That Touches Pitch Shall Be Defiled

scenes.setting: A careful loop back to the kill site: no trace, no memory in the passersby — only the boundary-feel of a Sealed Artifact spanning at least a block; the 'never perform unprepared' rule stirs the potion's characteristics
scenes.text_anchor: There was nothing out of the ordinary about his target area.

scenes.setting: Dinner ambush at Jurgen's: with Doris hospitalized, the lawyer's own blackened cooking must be survived politely ('the white bread isn't bad' — 'That was bought from Dodge bakery'); Klein is hired at two soli a visit to feed Brody, who promptly turns his back on him
scenes.text_anchor: “That was bought from Dodge bakery.”

scenes.setting: Home to a stampless letter: Isengard confirms the murderer found and killed — half the bounty coming; with Backlund easing, Klein plans to seek Sharron and Maric's mysticism books through Kaspars
scenes.text_anchor: “… I'm very pleased to inform you that the murderer has been found and killed on the spot.

scenes.setting: Bravehearts Bar under new management: Kaspars driven out by a gang Klein suspects is a Rose School trap — and the usurper boss is found hanging in billiard room 3 with a dead-knotted rope
scenes.text_anchor: “Boss is dead!”

scenes.setting: Behind the bar, a human slaughterhouse: scattered limbs, intestines on the wall, deep claw gouges — werewolf work; the trap-layers took their pound of flesh, confirming Sharron and Maric as Rose School defectors
scenes.text_anchor: It was like a thick and sharp claw that forcefully scratched out a mark!

scenes.setting: A brown carriage halts before him: Maric and Sharron inside; asked for deep mysticism texts (Shaman King Klarman's Book of Secrets among them), Sharron names her price in two words — 'Help. We'll use your help as barter.'
scenes.text_anchor: “We'll use your help as barter.”

scenes.setting: In the moving carriage, the defectors' story: an ancient Southern-Continent order fallen to bloody indulgence — Sharron and Maric's creed of repression against it; the price of their Book of Secrets is joining a hunt to kill the Sequence 5 pursuer with the Sharron-restraining Sealed Artifact — Maric first bait, Sharron second, Klein the hunter with the 'eye'
scenes.text_anchor: “Our philosophy is to repress and show temperance.”

scenes.setting: The Accursed pathway laid bare: Prisoner, Lunatic, Werewolf, Zombie (Maric), Wraith (Sharron) — each with its full-moon curse; the target is Wraith Steve wearing the Scarlet Lunar Corona with Zombie Jason and Werewolf Tyre beside him; spoils split — characteristic to Maric, Corona to Sharron, the rest plus the Book of Secrets to Klein
scenes.text_anchor: “That cursed artifact that needs to be sealed is called ‘Scarlet Lunar Corona.'

scenes.setting: Shaman King Klarman's Book of Secrets described — mysticism enough to make an expert of anyone; Klein asks for a day, swears secrecy on Rosago's Notary Certificate under Sharron's seal of light, and steps off the zombie-driven carriage
scenes.text_anchor: “I promise I won't tell anyone what I just learned from Miss Sharron and Mr. Maric.”

scenes.setting: Decoy divinations downstairs, the real ones at 4 a.m. above the fog (Dark Emperor card politely flipped face-down): accept, considerable but survivable danger — 'Then, let's have a grand performance.'
scenes.text_anchor: Then, let's have a grand performance.

scenes.setting: Nine o'clock, an empty living room: Klein accepts aloud to the oriel window and asks for preparation days; a bodiless voice answers 'Okay. After you've finished preparing, you can pay the bar a visit.'
scenes.text_anchor: “After you've finished preparing, you can pay the bar a visit.”

scenes.setting: Glaint's study: a Psychology Alchemists-adjacent gathering is on for this afternoon in North Borough; Glaint tags along, proud owner of the Apothecary formula — sold to him by Fors at a tidy 70-pound markup
scenes.text_anchor: “Oh, Fors sold it to me. 300 pounds.

scenes.setting: The corpse-pool gathering at the derelict medical school: ghost stories terrorize poor Glaint, a hooked corpse's slit abdomen speaks 'Let the gathering begin' — and Audrey's public bid for the Spectator formula finds no seller but many eyes
scenes.text_anchor: “Let the gathering begin.”

scenes.setting: Homeward with a tail: Xio senses the tracker; Audrey deduces it is the Psychology Alchemists vetting her, stages a natural noble's return through Glaint's mansion, and waits — nervous and hopeful — for their approach
scenes.text_anchor: “It seems like someone is following us!”

scenes.setting: Klein's 'preparations': two ordinary days of club cards with Talim and cat-feeding duty — then Friday, eight o'clock, iron mask on, into Eye of Wisdom's activity room
scenes.text_anchor: he put on his iron mask and wore his black-hooded robe

scenes.setting: Friday's gathering: the Apothecary hunts a tame Beyonder beast (new Sequence showing); Klein trades the Dark Emperor card's Barbarian formula for fifty purifying/demon-hunting/exorcism bullets plus revolver, fishes for Sun-domain relics — and someone asks for an adult Black Widow Spider Silk Gland: a Demoness of Pleasure ingredient
scenes.text_anchor: “Fifty bullets for 500 pounds or the Barbarian potion formula.

scenes.setting: The gathering winds down: nobody has the Black Widow gland (Klein resists tailing the male buyer of a Demoness ingredient), and the Apothecary sells out his medicines in three minutes
scenes.text_anchor: no one responded.

scenes.setting: Prepared at last, into 32 Verdi Street at night: a strangled burglar's ghost-theater loops the staircase — until Azik's whistle is thrown as bait and one pale-gold purifying bullet burns the wraith away ('Bye bye'); the basement holds the brown notebook from the divination dream
scenes.text_anchor: The pale gold purifying bullet flew out and accurately hit that cold and indistinct object.

scenes.setting: The basement notebook: the Abraham family — Tudor-era titans cursed since ancestor Bethel vanished in the War of the Four Emperors, every Beyonder generation losing control (Mr. Door's full-moon cries?); it yields the Apprentice, Trickmaster and ASTROLOGER formulas before its author's fatal full-moon advancement
scenes.text_anchor: “Sequence 9. Apprentice… “Sequence 8. Trickmaster… “Sequence 7. Astrologer…”

scenes.setting: Home via East Borough, formulas verified above the fog — then a staged prayer from The World (in a mocked-up 'ordinary room') is beamed to Miss Magician: the Trickmaster formula, hers for Sun-domain purification items
scenes.text_anchor: “Please tell Miss Magician that I've already obtained the Trickmaster potion formula.

chapters_detail.title: The Search For A Missing Person

scenes.setting: Fors, marking the next full moon on her calendar, receives The World's offer through the fog — the Trickmaster formula at last! — then hides her secret-society joy behind a half-truth when Xio comes home
scenes.text_anchor: The Trickmaster formula that I've been arduously searching for all these years

scenes.setting: Bounty day at Isengard's: 1000 pounds split, and 'expert at deduction' Sherlock Moriarty takes the top share of 300; then Stuart hands over a missing-person flyer — the vanished man is one Emlyn White
scenes.text_anchor: “I declare that Detective Sherlock Moriarty will be awarded 300 pounds!”

scenes.setting: Duke Negan's tea party: Lady Norma, Duchess Della's sister, corners Audrey by the bathroom — 'I heard our beautiful young lady is very interested in mysticism?' The Psychology Alchemists' test begins
scenes.text_anchor: “I heard that our beautiful young lady is very interested in mysticism?”

scenes.setting: Lady Norma arranges tomorrow's tea with her 'mysticism experts' — the Telepathist reads her recruiter's nerves and walks off in a proud straight line
scenes.text_anchor: “How about we have our afternoon tea together tomorrow?”

scenes.setting: Klein declines the Emlyn White job unasked and gets walked out by Isengard himself, trading warnings about the Devil's possible master and accents — Sivellaus meets Midseashire
scenes.text_anchor: “There might be an even more ferocious guy hiding behind the killer's back.

scenes.setting: Above the fog, courting death again: divining the Master Key's full-moon face — a scalp-peeling ancient-Hermes 'requesting assistance': Mr. Door's plea is baked into the curse itself
scenes.text_anchor: “What it manifests during the full moon.”

scenes.setting: A pass by the bar (Kaspars is back), then Sharron materializes in the carriage: her mystical item is ready; Klein offers the Apothecary's sedative for Maric's full-moon agony — test it tomorrow night, triple-dose before the battle
scenes.text_anchor: “I have a different kind of sedative here, from that Apothecary.”

scenes.setting: The carriage deal closes: sedative handed over, battleground candidates to be circled on a map left on his coffee table — Klein quietly planning escape routes in case allies turn on him
scenes.text_anchor: “Prepare a map of Backlund when you're back.

scenes.setting: Cat-sitting duty at the dark Jurgen house: boiled chicken breast for Brody, one-sided conversation included — the black cat just stares
scenes.text_anchor: Klein squatted down and tried to touch Brody's head

scenes.setting: Tea at Lady Norma's: 'mysticism experts' Hilbert Alucard and baby-faced psychiatrist Escalante Oseleka probe the girl who plays perfect novice; the parting hint — become a psychiatrist before marriage — reads as the next stage of the Psychology Alchemists' vetting
scenes.text_anchor: “This is Miss Escalante Oseleka. She's a doctor for mental health

scenes.setting: Sunday: the circled map memorized building by building; at the club a cheerful Aaron credits the Goddess (via a Nightmare-assisted Nighthawk ritual, Klein privately notes) — and urges Sherlock to convert
scenes.text_anchor: “Put your faith in the Goddess!”

scenes.setting: Faith firmly not for changing, Will Auceptin unseen since discharge; then Mary and Stelyn arrive for tennis — and Stelyn, satisfied with the detective's earnings, invites him to next Sunday's party stocked with 'excellent unmarried ladies'
scenes.text_anchor: “There will be a lot of unmarried ladies at the party

scenes.setting: Full-moon rescue above the fog, then awkward silence broken by Fors's life story: the Abraham widow who walked through walls, the deathbed formula and glowing characteristic, and the bracelet that made the ravings worse
scenes.text_anchor: “Honorable Mr. Fool, you have saved me once again.”

scenes.setting: Monday morning's one-word note on the coffee table — 'Effective.' — and at a quarter to three, up to the fog for the next Tarot gathering
scenes.text_anchor: “Effective.”

scenes.setting: Gathering with the Dark Emperor card casually on display: Audrey privately reports the Psychology Alchemists' approach (and pays diary pages of… Roselle's constipation) learning the card's name; Alger probes a revived slave trade and wants Wind-blessed; Derrick asks advice for the Fallen Creator temple mission under Elder Lovia
scenes.text_anchor: “That is the Dark Emperor card.

scenes.setting: The Sun describes the half-destroyed temple and the unique statue standing in it, and old fox Alger milks the description for free before giving his advice on the expedition: absolutely do not go, because a true evil god's temple stays dangerous long after it falls
scenes.text_anchor: “The Fallen Creator is a true evil god.

scenes.setting: Klein notes sourly that Alger reached the same answer he would have, without paying for the description — then the Hanged Man coaches Derrick to fake the brink of losing control to dodge Lovia's compulsory expedition, 'you are doing so to save the City of Silver'
scenes.text_anchor: “You can always pretend to be on the brink of losing control.

scenes.setting: The free-discussion tail: sea stories from Alger seed Fors's next pirate romance before The Fool adjourns and naps
scenes.text_anchor: Klein, whose spirituality was gradually drained, announced the end of the Tarot Gathering.

scenes.setting: Mr. A's gathering, subtly wrong — the mountain now a reared snake: Fors's Sun-domain request draws a 9000-pound Band of Light offer; relayed through the fog, The World declines the believer-making ring and sells her Trickmaster for 450 in cash
scenes.text_anchor: “Pay 450 pounds and you'll get the formula for Trickmaster.”

scenes.setting: After the guests go: Mr. A collapses on the basement stairs, flesh melting into a skinless shadow-double before reflowing — then kneels sobbing in confession for the Lord's failed descent
scenes.text_anchor: His flesh and blood melted and mixed into the shadow

scenes.setting: City of Silver: torn between honor and survival, Derrick chooses Alger's plan — and begins draining his spirituality to fake the brink of losing control
scenes.text_anchor: He began practicing the Light Suppliant's Beyonder powers to drain his spirituality

scenes.setting: The art studio: Countess Caitlyn arranges Escalante as psychology tutor twice a week — exactly as the Psychology Alchemists intended, exactly as Audrey hoped; Klein meanwhile confirms tomorrow's gathering and takes a day off
scenes.text_anchor: “She recommended a psychiatrist named Escalante.

scenes.setting: At the club: Talim's darker follow-up — 'do you know rare people with strange abilities?' — is swallowed unanswered, and Mike Joseph's bodyguard job is teased for the day after tomorrow
scenes.text_anchor: “Sherlock, do you know—do you know rare people who have strange abilities and are very powerful?”

scenes.setting: In a sealed club lounge above the fog: Fors's 450 pounds pass the illusory door, and the Trickmaster formula settles into her mind — years of searching over
scenes.text_anchor: “Sequence 8. Trickmaster.

scenes.setting: Spending lavishly at Wednesday's gathering: the Briber formula sold for 900 cash (the Holy Sunbird whip declined), then 2000 pounds down for Eye of Wisdom's Grade 2 Sealed Artifact — the Sun Brooch 'Midsummer', nemesis of the undead, price of perpetual heat
scenes.text_anchor: “2,000 pounds. I want that Sun Brooch.”

scenes.setting: The Sun Brooch changes hands: instant desert heat, a headful of Sun-domain spells (Holy Light, Holy Water, Fire of Light, Holy Oath…), 2000 pounds counted thrice — and Eye of Wisdom sends the big spender out first, safe from greedy eyes
scenes.text_anchor: he saw the sky filled with dancing dots of pure gold light

scenes.setting: In the hired carriage Sharron confirms preparations are done — and takes Klein's odd request to have Kaspars bury a box of explosives across the battlefield: 'I just want to put on some fireworks'
scenes.text_anchor: “I just want to put on some fireworks.”

scenes.setting: Thursday: Mike Joseph invites himself to toast and milk, hiring protection for a sponsored exposé of East Borough — answer tomorrow; then a note materializes on the coffee table: 'Tonight at 10 o'clock. The back door of Bravehearts Bar.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Tonight at 10 o'clock. We'll meet at the back door of Bravehearts Bar.”

scenes.setting: Ten o'clock pickup: sedatives handed over (two and a half tubes, Maric judges), purification quirks confirmed, and the trio reaches the abandoned West Balam dock — Maric's zombies sleep beneath the ambush ground; 'the simpler the plan, the more effective it is'
scenes.text_anchor: “We're on the way there.”

scenes.setting: The stage is set: All-Black Eye buried center-field under a spirit cage, explosives seeded through warehouses, a top-hatted paper double posted in a gap, Sun Brooch pinned on — and from a rooftop shadow the sweating Magician watches three figures approach
scenes.text_anchor: Is this the state every magician is in before he goes onstage?

scenes.setting: The ambush inverts: Tyre carries the Scarlet Lunar Corona (Steve predicted the plan), Sharron collapses weakened but opens her Door of Mysteries on frenzied Jason; sedated Maric holds on — and Klein's All-Black Eye finds the invisible Steve about to possess Maric: decoy explosion, then a Cleave-charged purifying bullet fires
scenes.text_anchor: Wraith Steve! He wants to possess Maric!

scenes.setting: Wraith Steve revealed and furious: his possession gaze nearly claims Klein (saved by Holy Light and a burning paper double); explosive finger-snaps redirect the thrown Scarlet Lunar Corona, shield Sharron, and blast Jason through her Door of Mysteries — gone as if never born — while Steve's scream of rage hammers every skull on the field
scenes.text_anchor: the mysterious and illusory door closed with a clang, devouring the rest of his screams

scenes.setting: Steve's Biological Poison Bottle sickens the field — but the Sun Brooch dilutes it, and Klein's masterstroke lands: a bullet unearths the whistle-and-Master-Key ring, the undead riot for it, and grabbing it feeds Steve the Master Key's full-moon curse-scream; the freed Scarlet Lunar Corona is flicked to Sharron, her bronze Door reopens on Steve, and six holy bullets hammer his burning head
scenes.text_anchor: a faint but very strange sound entered his mind, ripping at his nerves and scraping his scalp

scenes.setting: The finish: eight holy bullets into one cheekbone, Sharron possessing the charred Steve to pulp his own head, her blood-vine devouring his fleeing phantom, and one final snapped-finger firework shredding what remained; Tyre dies twisting off his own head, spoils are split (Poison Bottle and fang to Klein), and the Book of Secrets already waits in his room
scenes.text_anchor: “I still have lots of fireworks which I haven't released.”

scenes.setting: Match-to-match Flaming Jumps out of the dock, paint wiped, cane retrieved — and a serene alibi in Lever Cathedral's third pew while the Machinery Hivemind frowns over a scrubbed battlefield
scenes.text_anchor: Klein sat in the third pew along the aisle.

scenes.setting: Past midnight home: the goatskin Book of Secrets found in the wardrobe, every dangerous spoil thrown above the fog, and an exhausted Magician asleep in ten seconds
scenes.text_anchor: “Book of Secrets. “Klarman.”

scenes.setting: At the scrubbed battlefield, deacon Ikanser Bernard consults the mirror Arrodes: blurred visions of the top-hatted bower, the cloaked man, the transparent-faced woman — then the mirror demands its reciprocal question: 'What's your sexual orientation?'
scenes.text_anchor: “Respected Arrodes, my question is ‘Who were the participants in the incident that just happened here?'”

scenes.setting: Six a.m. above the fog (visions only: Tyre's werewolf feats; the Poison Bottle's random horrors and amber antidote): the spoils are appraised, and the Book of Secrets opens on its creed — 'We worship the moon, not the Evernight Goddess.'
scenes.text_anchor: “We worship the moon, not the Evernight Goddess.”

scenes.setting: Reading Klarman's creed: two isolated continents both worshiped the 'primitive moon' over the Goddess — a hidden power worth circumventing; Klein plans to mine the book's ritual structures for his own King-of-Yellow-and-Black system
scenes.text_anchor: “The one and only red moon, the symbol of life and beauty, the mother of all spiritual forces.”

scenes.setting: A head cold from carrying the Poison Bottle, a hundred pounds of bullets mourned over a fried egg — then Mike Joseph arrives for the East Borough job and gets dressed down, literally, into worker's clothes
scenes.text_anchor: “Sir, you'd better change into something a little worse

scenes.setting: The greasy corner coffee shop: Klein's old 'interviewee' again — now dock-laboring, renting a sleeping spot at six and a half pence a week — while Mike's pen races across his notepad
scenes.text_anchor: “Mr. Reporter, it's you?”

chapters_detail.title: Today Is Quite Different From Yesterday

scenes.setting: The coffee-shop interview: a ruined grain merchant's widow tells her story with a dead calm, eats politely, asks to sleep — and quietly dies in the warm chair; 'at least she filled her stomach', says Old Kohler, newly hired as guide
scenes.text_anchor: “She's dead.”

scenes.setting: The policeman shrugs at the death but hunts for illegal firearms — finding nothing on the Magician whose revolver sits unseen under the table; the interview plan is redrawn by lodging and shift, and the trio heads for a nearby apartment
scenes.text_anchor: “I suspect that you're carrying a gun illegally!

chapters_detail.title: Tales of an Adventure in East Borough

scenes.setting: The East Borough 'adventure': six-year-old thieves, gang territories mapped by Old Kohler, tool-sharing watch craftsmen packed in one apartment, and laundry girls too busy surviving to be interviewed — 1.35 million people in the jungle
scenes.text_anchor: “This place is closer to the jungle than to human society.

scenes.setting: City of Silver: 'losing control' Derrick is escorted to the spire's underground quarantine — where a shrill 'Help!' rings from a sealed room and cuts to silence
scenes.text_anchor: “Help!” A sharp shrill voice suddenly sounded from a sealed room.

scenes.setting: The spire's quarantine cells: a neighbor is purged mid-scream; through the far wall a forty-two-year prisoner — an old exploration captain — recounts finding the first outsider in 2000 years, whose escort ended in every teammate losing control. His name: 'Amon.'
scenes.text_anchor: “He told us that his name was…” … “Amon.”

scenes.setting: Two more days of East Borough: ten to a bedroom, floor-space sold in day and night shifts, filth without sewers — Mike's manuscript grows heavier and the reporter grows quieter
scenes.text_anchor: “… Squalid, crowded, smelly—that's the most objective impression.

scenes.setting: The factory district finale: unmasked women breathing lead dust, textile workers massing to smash the machines taking their jobs — Mike leaves silent and ten pounds lighter, and Klein retains Old Kohler as his East Borough informant at a pound a week
scenes.text_anchor: “These factory owners are murderers!”

scenes.setting: Psychology lessons with Escalante: dangled hints about mysticism 'seminars' met with practiced naivety; afterwards Susie's verdict — 'She's not sincere!' — though the material beats meat and biscuits
scenes.text_anchor: “She's not sincere!” Susie answered flatly.

scenes.setting: Stelyn's matchmaking banquet: incomes announced to the ladies' faces (Jurgen the clear favorite over a scruffy detective), invented case stories for the twins — and news that Mary's council luncheon invitation comes from Hibbert Hall himself
scenes.text_anchor: “This is Mr. Sherlock Moriarty, a well-known detective.

scenes.setting: Monday at the Hall villa: the Sammers among nobility; on the balcony Stelyn asks the angelic girl what such a fine hound costs — Audrey glances at Susie and smiles: '450 pounds'
scenes.text_anchor: “450 pounds.”

scenes.setting: The carriage home from the villa: Luke talks council politics while Stelyn stares out the window, '450 pounds' for a dog ringing in her ears
scenes.text_anchor: “A trained hound is priced between 450 and 700 pounds.”

scenes.setting: The quarantine cell: Mr. Fool's summons arrives inside the spire's seal; as red light swallows Derrick, the old captain's knocking signal on the wall goes unanswered — then hesitates into silence
scenes.text_anchor: “Prepare for the gathering.”

scenes.setting: Count Hall's ajar study: Susie reads the title aloud — a Church-commissioned survey of East Borough's living conditions, investigator one Mike Joseph — someone else is pushing the same cause Audrey wanted
scenes.text_anchor: “Survey of living conditions at all levels in East Borough, the dock area, and the factory district.

scenes.setting: The gathering opens on Derrick's worry about being watched, and Mr. Fool confirms that some mystical items do carry such effects — relief enough for The Sun to give up one of the City of Silver's top secrets
scenes.text_anchor: “It's one of the City of Silver's top secrets.”

scenes.setting: Then the question the former captain left him with, blurted out to the whole table — and Klein, who knows exactly where he has heard that name, says nothing and lets The Hanged Man answer instead
scenes.text_anchor: “Have any of you heard of a person named Amon?”

scenes.setting: Alger unpacks the taboo: Amon — most mysterious of the five Tudor founding families, blasphemers who usurp gods' powers, self-styled descendants of an ancient Sun God; his advice to Derrick: probe the old captain, but that survivor himself is deeply wrong
scenes.text_anchor: “The Amons are a family of blasphemers, and they wield the secrets to usurp the powers of deities!

scenes.setting: Justice's private exchange: three fresh diary pages traded for one revelation — 'Sequence 0, Dark Emperor' — plus a week's secrecy so Miss Magician never connects Audrey to Justice
scenes.text_anchor: “Mr. Fool, I have another three new pages of Roselle's diary.”

scenes.setting: Diary-reading interlude, the very first entries: 'I am now Roselle Gustav… my real name: Huang Tao' — a mysterious silver plate before crossing, Tik Tok homesickness — dated mere months from Klein's own transmigration, yet two hundred years apart in this world
scenes.text_anchor: “I am now Roselle Gustav, but I'll never forget my real name.

scenes.setting: The interlude ends on hope and worry: two hundred years here may equal one year back home — and young Roselle's diary records a four-eyed monster battle and his resolve to crack the silver plate's symbols himself
scenes.text_anchor: “This world might be a little different from what I know it to be.

scenes.setting: Free trading: Fors's ingredient shopping runs into the Beyonder-poverty wall ('any good ways of earning money?' — silence); The World lists his Faceless ingredients, and Alger posts a bounty on the slave-trader 'Baelen' with the missing third tooth
scenes.text_anchor: “Everyone, do you have any good ways of earning money?”

scenes.setting: Back in the dark cell, Derrick taps the wall signal — no answer through the metal; then an elderly, fleeting voice speaks from the bed behind him: 'Are you looking for me…'
scenes.text_anchor: “Are you looking for me…”

scenes.setting: The voice behind him: the old captain mutated — head split in halves, wounds full of speaking teeth ('Look, am I not normal…'); Derrick's prayed pillar of light births a featureless man of light who melts the horror, until a monocled phantom in a pointed hat flashes and everything whites out
scenes.text_anchor: “Look, am I not normal…”

scenes.setting: Chief Colin Iliad, bone-sword in hand over a ten-ringed translucent worm: the captain was deliberate bait to expose Amon's design, and Derrick's Sun pathway triggered it; released home, Derrick reports all to Mr. Fool — and in his sleep his finger taps the bed: once, twice, thrice…
scenes.text_anchor: “It was close…”

scenes.setting: Post-gathering planning: the Magician's missing rules must be found fast — audience applause as digestion fuel to be tested — when layered illusory pleas interrupt
scenes.text_anchor: he heard a series of illusory, stacked pleas.

scenes.setting: Above the fog (visions only: The Sun's prayer image with a monocled, python-coiled phantom riding his spirit): Amon is stowing away toward the gray fog itself — so Klein adapts the Book of Secrets' Blood Moon Sacrifice into a secret-deed ritual of the King of Yellow and Black, and tasks the unwitting Derrick with performing it
scenes.text_anchor: By residing in the Spirit Body of The Sun, he is waiting for the next Tarot Gathering

scenes.setting: In the City of Silver, Derrick bleeds himself for ink, paints The Fool's name and symbols on monster hide, and begins the chant — spirituality flowing into the crimson script
scenes.text_anchor: he used his own blood as ink, and he wrote the name of The Fool

scenes.setting: The whole fog trembles as the secret deed connects: the python-phantom lifts its monocled head, hunting the hidden channel — and Klein's eyes stop on the Sun Brooch
scenes.text_anchor: his gaze stopped at the Sun Brooch.

scenes.setting: The counter-exorcism: fog-power poured through the Sun Brooch condenses a golden figure — too chaotic at 10% strength, until the Dark Emperor card's high-level authority steadies it into a twelve-black-winged colossus that blasts Amon's skeletal grasping hand off the crimson star's boundary
scenes.text_anchor: on its back, it grew pairs of enormous pitch-black wings. There were a total of twelve pairs!

scenes.setting: Derrick basks in the City of Silver's first successful secret deed in two millennia, receives Sun-domain knowledge — then is shown what had been coiled around his spirit: 'Praise you, the mighty Mr. Fool!'
scenes.text_anchor: “Praise you, the mighty Mr. Fool!”

scenes.setting: Somewhere in the deep darkness, above a ravine and a rotting one-eyed giant: the real Amon pinches his crystal monocle, smiles — 'As expected… The Fool.' — and leaps into the dark
scenes.text_anchor: “As expected…” … “The Fool.”

scenes.setting: Threat eliminated, urgency doubled: a mere clone was this terrifying — the Magician's remaining rules must be found, and fast
scenes.text_anchor: For a mere clone to be so bizarre and terrifying, one can imagine how powerful his main body is…
